page: Microsoft Azure HB120rs_v3 is a high-performance computing instance within the HBv3 series, engineered for tightly coupled computational tasks. Powered by x86_64 architecture processors running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 120 dedicated vCPUs along with 456.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes an allocation ratio of 3.8 GB of RAM per vCPU, matching the requirements of memory-bound simulation codes, mathematical modeling, and distributed engineering workflows.

Storage configuration includes 2435 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, providing low-latency scratch space for intermediate data files and large transient datasets. The instance also supports Azure Premium Storage and includes native RDMA network capabilities, which facilitate low-latency inter-node communication across multi-instance clusters without relying on standard software networking overhead. Accelerated graphics hardware is omitted, with zero GPUs present on the instance.

Cost efficiency is anchored in its dense compute configuration, maximizing processor core density and RDMA interconnect throughput within a single node. Because the server does not include complementary public IPv4 addresses or graphics processing units, network routing and visualization tasks require separate infrastructure planning. The platform is structured specifically for parallel processing workloads, including computational fluid dynamics, weather forecasting, finite element analysis, and high-throughput computational workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure HB120rs_v3 is a High Performance Computing series virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 120 dedicated vCPUs and 456.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.8 GB of memory per core. Designed for high-throughput computational workloads, the server integrates 2435 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and includes support for RDMA networking and Premium Storage. It does not bundle GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, focusing physical resources entirely on raw processing density and interconnect performance. This allocation profile delivers cost-effective scaling for multi-node MPI clusters, computational fluid dynamics, seismic processing, molecular dynamics, and large-scale engineering simulations that require fast local disk access alongside dense x86 execution cores.
